_README: Hand-maintained list of players known, from PUBLIC REPORTING, to have
signed a multi-year contract or extension while they were still
pre-arbitration. This exists because of a hard limit measured while
building scripts/salary_estimates.py: the MLB Stats API /transactions
feed -- the same feed the service-time engine already reads, and the
only mechanism the brief for this feature proposed -- records ROSTER
STATUS, not money. An extension changes no roster status, so it is
never logged there. Measured 2026-10-29 against every cached
transaction file in data/cache/transactions/ (the whole rostered
population): zero rows anywhere contain the word 'extension' or a
contract-year phrase. Michael Harris II signed an 8-year extension in
August 2022 and his cached transaction history has no trace of it.
So this file is the second signal, in the same spirit as
data/reference_super_two.json and data/reference_service_time.json:
entered by a person from public reporting (team announcements, AP,
ESPN, MLB.com), never scraped from Spotrac/Cot's/Baseball-Reference or
any other salary site, and never carrying a dollar figure or contract
length here -- only the fact that a deal exists, which is all the
salary estimate needs to know in order to stay silent.
THIS LIST IS NOT EXHAUSTIVE. It cannot be: there is no free, permitted,
machine-readable feed of contract extensions, which is the same gap
that keeps the contract tool's Module B/C unbuilt (see CLAUDE.md). A
name missing here does not mean no extension exists -- it means nobody
has entered one yet. The owner is in clubhouses and will know about a
teammate's deal well before any public report does, which is exactly
why this is a file he can edit directly rather than something scraped.
ADD A ROW THE MOMENT YOU HEAR ABOUT A PRE-ARB EXTENSION, even before
it is public. Each row needs: id (the MLB person id -- the same one in
docs/data/service_time.json, never a jersey number or anything else),
name (for human readability only; matching is by id), signed (the date
if known, else null), and note (where this came from). Review the
current pre-arb list periodically: run
`python3 -c "import json; db=json.load(open('docs/data/service_time.json'));
[print(p['id'], p['name'], p['team']) for p in db['players'] if p['on_40_man']
and p['service_days_total'] and not p['free_agent_eligible'] and not
p['arbitration_eligible'] and not p['super_two_candidate']]"` and check
each name against what you know.

name: Julio Rodríguez
note: Long-term extension signed with the Mariners while pre-arbitration. Widely reported at the time (AP/ESPN). Kept as a worked example and a regression test -- he has since crossed into arbitration eligibility on service time alone, so the pre-arb gate already excludes him regardless of this entry.
source: public reporting, hand-entered, not independently verified against a primary document
